text: Humboldt’s larger American project remained unfinished, although he left substantial grammatical studies, including a Nahuatl grammar (modern manuscript-based edition, 1994). The Nahuatl dictionary, published in 2000, was conceived by Humboldt but compiled and revised chiefly by Eduard Buschmann, who continued the work after Humboldt’s death.

sources.supports: Unfinished American project and substantial descriptive manuscripts

sources.reference: Jürgen Trabant 2002, L’édition des oeuvres linguistiques de Humboldt : le sort d’un legs intempestif, sections 4.1–4.2
sources.supports: Nahuatl grammar; dictionary conception, compilation and posthumous continuation
Manuscript-based grammar edition in 1994 and dictionary edition in 2000

editorial_scope: Historical translator commentary, distinct from Humboldt’s wording. Modern edition dates do not imply that he published these works during his lifetime.
